phase2_design_signals: Two honest rung-2 duration failures with clean mechanics are stronger design-review input than one pass would have been: they isolate the variable (scope sizing) because throughput, governance overhead, and interrupt mechanics replicated across both attempts.

The safe-hold-trigger principle emerged from sponsor experience of being measured ('the answer should take however long it takes'), not from agent-side failure — evidence that interrupt-protocol design needs the human's lived experience, not only transport telemetry.

Mission 022's agent kept waiting past the named timeout and correctly applied the answer that arrived at T+734s; the rule as written was violated while the behavior was right, which is the clearest possible signal the rule encoded the wrong concept.
